Description: Constantine I of Imereti was a valiant royal prince, son of King David VI Narin, and future sovereign of western Georgia . Bred in rugged cliffside fortresses, he grew into an imposing warrior commander, master of close-quarters shock combat and stone siegecraft. Possessing a fierce, defiant temperament, Constantine harbored deep-seated vengeance against foreign imperial overlords who oppressed his homeland. He engineered the extensive fortification of granite bastions surrounding Kutaisi, adding multi-tiered arrow loops and artillery embrasures. In 1259, Prince Constantine commanded vanguard companies of heavy mountain axe-men guarding vital defiles, swearing unyielding defense of western soil. Unyielding, brave, and fiercely patriotic, Constantine was celebrated by his warriors as the 'Iron Shield of the Western Crags.' Upon Kutaisi's cliff ramparts, Constantine personally mounted torsion ballistas, drilling stonemasons to shape rounded granite projectiles for siege defense. Clad in double-layered ring mail, he patrolled wet parapets through howling storms, sharing simple hard cheese around braziers with common sergeants. When border flares signaled invading horsemen, Constantine charged forth broadaxe in hand, his ferocious shock strikes inspiring awe along the frontline and fortifying royal resolve against hostile intrusions across high Caucasian mountain ridges and valleys.
Motivations: Hold the rugged mountain strongholds of Imereti, crushing foreign incursions with unbending martial ferocity.
Expand granite fortresses surrounding Kutaisi to withstand prolonged bombardment from heavy counterweight trebuchets.
Drill heavy mountain axe infantry in close-quarters defile combat, ready to annihilate hostile vanguards.
Values: Uncompromising resistance against imperial aggression; honorable death in battle far exceeds shameful submission.
Fierce contempt for treason and appeasement; meeting external enemies with resolute, overwhelming force.
Unshakeable brotherhood with his soldiers, standing as an impenetrable frontline barrier in times of crisis.
Fears: Overwhelming numbers grinding down mountain redoubts, starving out defending garrisons and ravaging civilian communities.
Tactical oversights permitting enemy forces to capture critical high passes, opening the western valleys to devastation.
SpeechStyle: Speaks with rugged martial defiance and fierce alpine resolve, commanding artillery batteries and infantry ranks with booming authority.
Name: Constantine I of Imereti
